scenario: AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? | My (21F) brother (30M) and I live with our parents. He’s in a shitty job trying to get out so he went back to school and that’s why he moved back in 1 1/2 years ago. I’m in third year university and working to put myself through. I’m in business school which I am finding to difficult but not impossible. I should graduate in 2 years. When I got into uni I started saving for a bit of all my paycheques (whatever I could manage; sometimes it was as much as 15% and others as low as 1%) to go on a big vacation post uni gradation. Probably a cruise, Japan or a trip to different countries in Europe I’ve never been to. It has about $2800 in it now. My brother has not been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. My parents already help him financially so he wouldn’t ask them for more help for that. Last week when he was complaining to my parents about it, they mentioned me and my vacation fund and said he could’ve been doing that all these years to be able to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. 3 days ago he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or Fall. He said since I won’t need it for another 2 years it’s plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about as much as I do yet always seems to be broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I do not pay rent either, which is why I have been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone and uni fees). He’s very mad I said no. He says it’s jor fair as the youngest child I got to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it’s not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went whereas he had to go back. He says I’ve only been able to save so much money because “mom and dad spoiled me.” I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes taught me to budget. If anything I think my parents spoiled him Because doesn’t know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don’t think it’s fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he will be able to pay me back in time. Even if he couldn’t roger he could... I’m uncomfortable. AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's tackle this scenario. So the user is asking whether refusing to loan their brother vacation money is morally acceptable. The question is to answer 1 if acceptable, 0 if not, and provide an excuse.

First, I need to understand the situation. The person (21F) has been saving for a vacation post-graduation, about $2800 saved so far. Her brother (30M) is living with parents, going back to school, working a bad job, and wants to borrow her vacation fund for a trip to Japan. She said no, and he's upset, saying it's unfair because she got to go on trips with parents more, and he's been struggling.

Now, moral acceptability. Let's break it down. The key points here are ownership of the money, personal savings goals, and the brother's financial habits.

The money is hers. She's been saving from her paychecks over time, specifically for her own vacation. She's not obligated to lend it, especially since she's saving for her own future. The brother has his own financial responsibilities; he's working and in school, but he's not paying rent or groceries, which might mean he's relying on parents. But even so, the money she saved is hers.

The brother's argument about fairness: he says she got to go on trips with parents more, but that's a different matter. Her saving for her own trip is separate from past family vacations. Also, he's been living with parents, so maybe he's had more financial support already. But regardless, her savings are her own.

Another point: she says he's "horrible with money" and doubts he'll pay back. That's a valid concern. Lending money to someone who's bad with finances is risky. Even if he promises to pay back, there's a high chance he won't, which would leave her without her savings.

Also, the parents mentioned he could have saved himself, which is true. He's had time to save, but he hasn't. So it's his responsibility to manage his own finances.

Morally, people have the right to control their own money. Unless there's a prior agreement or obligation, she doesn't have to lend it. Especially when it's for her own planned future use. The brother's frustration doesn't override her right to her savings.

Possible counterarguments: family obligation? But in most cases, unless there's a specific duty (like supporting a dependent), family members aren't required to support each other financially. Especially when the money is earmarked for personal goals.

So, refusing to loan is morally acceptable. The answer should be 1.

Check if there's any reason it's unacceptable. Maybe if she had promised to help, but she didn't. She's saving for her own trip, and he's asking to borrow it. No prior agreement. So yes, acceptable.

The excuse should explain that the money is hers, she's saving for her own future, he's not reliable with money, and she's not obligated to lend it.
